title: Public environmental data APIs
subtitle: Public weather and environmental data feed a product-shaped MCP server that exposes 21 tools, with a trimmed surface for a vendor agent platform.

stats.label: public data-service clients behind one server
MCP SDKs the same product was built on

lede: In the Auth and access plane I built a weather MCP server as a worked example of a product-shaped tool server, and the problem it solves is size. Public weather data is hourly, multi-variable and far larger than an assistant should read, and an assistant asked "can we pour concrete on Thursday?" needs a judgment. The advisory interprets conditions for field work, and saved locations let a user ask about "the north site". Behind it sit clients for national forecasts and alerts, climate history, wildfire incidents, an open global forecast service, precipitation radar, lightning detection and address geocoding. Public services differ in reliability, rate limits and response shape, so each client has its own cache, retries and timeouts.
quote: I decided the server would aggregate before it answers.
evidence: MCP server design: a product-shaped weather server over 9 public data-service clients that aggregates hourly data into daily answers and a construction-weather advisory.
Resilient third-party API integration: each public source with its own cache, retries and timeouts, so a failing service degrades only its part of an answer.
Microsoft Copilot Studio integration: 21 tools for desktop assistants and a trimmed Streamable-HTTP surface for Copilot Studio, the same product built on 2 MCP SDKs with 15 tool classes in .NET.
author: Corey James
